Question Choices: If p is prime is sqrt(p) rational or irrational?
Hints: A prime is not a perfect square.;Use the same contradiction argument as for sqrt(2).
Solution: A prime p is not a perfect square. If sqrt(p)=m/n in lowest terms, m^2=p n^2 implies p divides m. Substituting m=pk implies p divides n too, contradicting lowest terms. Thus sqrt(p) is irrational.

Solution: Yes. For rational a<b, choose c=a+(b-a)/sqrt(2). Because 0<1/sqrt(2)<1, a<c<b. The nonzero rational multiple of 1/sqrt(2) is irrational; adding rational a preserves irrationality.
